# Taṇhuppāda Sutta (Iti 105 (It 4.6 PTS It 109))

**ID:** Iti 105 (It 4.6 PTS It 109)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Taṇhuppāda Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Taṇhuppāda Sutta* ("The Arising of Craving", Iti 105) is the sixth discourse in the fourth section (Catukkanipāta) of the *Itivuttaka* [Windisch 1889]. The discourse identifies four grounds or occasions for the arising of craving in a monastic (*cattāro taṇhuppādā*): craving arising on account of robes (*cīvara-hetu*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta-hetu*), lodging (*senāsana-hetu*), and becoming or non-becoming (*itibhavābhava-hetu*) [Windisch 1889]. This prose teaching is concluded by a verse declaring that a person with craving as a companion (*taṇhādutiyo puriso*) wanders in *saṁsāra* for an extended duration and fails to transcend the round of existence, cycling between varied states of becoming (*itthabhāvaññathābhāvaṁ*) [Windisch 1889]. The textual formula regarding craving for states of existence (*itibhavābhavahetu taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati*) is also cited in Buddhist Sanskrit scholastic traditions, where the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* and its commentary analyze its equivalent (*itibhavavibhavahetos tṛṣṇā*) [de La Vallée Poussin, Abhidharmakośabhāṣyam].
